body: It probably shouldn't be a part of this PR
So we won't provide a `send` method? (bidirectional communication)

Kafka seems to have types - [`@types/kafkajs`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@types/kafkajs). You should be able to add the `import * as KafkaJS from 'kafkajs';` and then reference it `let kafkaPackage: KafkaJS | {} = {};`. TypeScript should then remove the `import` statement in the final bundle, since we are only using types. But you should double check, just to be sure :)

Kafka doesn't inherently support bidirectional communication (messaging pattern) through a single topic.  At least two topics would have to be created.  Even with two topics, the producer would have to know which partition(s) of the topic the consumer group is associated with.  See https://kafka.js.org/docs/producing#custom-partitioner

I could implement something like this but I would need to break out the logic for consumers and producers into something more granular.  These event "orchestrators" (lack of a better term) can be initialized and configured within class property decorators and `onModuleInit` and referenced by the decorators consuming messages and passed to the client methods producing messages.

So, I have just decided to avoid that for now and only added support for the async event pattern.

Was just using the other implementations as a reference and non of them use the third-party definitions.   Instead they all use an implicit any and NestJS implements it's own interface.  However, I would be more than happy to break existing convention and use third party types.  Also, kafkajs ships with its own definitions.
We can't use types because all transport packages are optional (and installed lazily on demand)

@kamilmysliwiec Are you sure? I did some investigations some time ago with `@nestjs/terminus` because I have had the same problem - I wanted to lazy load on demand, but keep type-security. I learned that TypeScript does not transpile  `import`-statements into the final JS file if the imported element is only used as type.
You can see in this [gist](https://gist.github.com/BrunnerLivio/e07f2210ecbd14f67c180b30df50b082) what I mean. In this example you still able to lazy load KafkaJS, but with types support.

I spent a lot of time trying to workaround this issue in TypeScript months ago (that's why we have `external` directory with types) so I'm pretty sure that it wasn't working before. Perhaps, something has changed in TS and now, it's possible - if so, we should add typings + remove this dir for other strategies as well
Alright. I think lets keep it in this PR as the other strategies, but challenge this in an additional PR. :)
